title: Progressive & Stationary Waves — MCQs
description: Topics: progressive wave definitions and mathematical form, stationary wave formation & expression, calculations (frequency, period, velocity, amplitude), and superposition of two progressive waves.

questions.q: Which best defines a progressive (traveling) wave?
options: A disturbance that moves through a medium transferring energy without net transport of matter
A standing pattern that does not transfer energy
A static deformation of a medium
questions.explanation: A progressive wave is a disturbance that travels through a medium carrying energy from one place to another, while the medium's particles oscillate about equilibrium.

questions.q: A progressive wave transfers:
questions.explanation: Progressive waves transport energy (and information), not mass (no net transport of matter in ideal waves).

questions.q: A common mathematical form of a one-dimensional progressive wave moving in +x direction is:
questions.explanation: General travelling wave: y = A sin(kx - ωt + φ) (moves in +x). For - sign reversed it moves in -x.

questions.q: In y = A sin(kx - ωt), the quantity k is the:
questions.explanation: k = 2π/λ is the wave number; ω = 2πf is angular frequency; λ is wavelength.

questions.q: Stationary (standing) waves are formed when:
options: Two progressive waves of same frequency and amplitude travel in opposite directions and superpose
questions.explanation: Standing waves form by superposition of two waves of same frequency, amplitude and speed traveling in opposite directions (usually same wavelength) so they interfere to produce nodes and antinodes.

questions.q: Which condition is NOT required to form a pure stationary wave?
questions.explanation: To form a stationary wave wavelengths must be equal; differing wavelengths do not produce simple stationary patterns.

questions.q: Superposing y1 = A sin(kx - ωt) and y2 = A sin(kx + ωt) gives stationary wave:
questions.explanation: Using trig identity: sin(α) + sin(β) = 2 sin((α+β)/2) cos((α-β)/2). Here results in y = 2A cos(kx) sin(ωt).

questions.q: In stationary wave y = 2A cos(kx) sin(ωt), nodes are at positions x satisfying:
questions.explanation: Nodes: cos(kx) = 0 ⇒ kx = (n+1/2)π ⇒ x = (2n+1)λ/4; amplitude factor 2A cos(kx) = 0.

questions.q: For a progressive wave y = 0.05 sin(4π x - 400π t) (SI units), the wavelength λ is:
questions.explanation: k = 4π ⇒ k = 2π/λ ⇒ λ = 2π / (4π) = 1/2? Wait: 2π/λ=4π ⇒ λ=1/2 m. (Select option matching calculation.)

Two progressive waves y1 = A sin(kx - ωt) and y2 = A sin(kx + ωt) superposed produce amplitude envelope 2A cos(kx). The maximum amplitude (at antinode) is:
questions.explanation: At antinode cos(kx)=±1 so maximum amplitude is 2A.

questions.q: Positions of nodes for stationary wave y = 2A cos(kx) sin(ωt) are at x = n λ/2
questions.explanation: Nodes occur where cos(kx)=0 ⇒ x = (2n+1)λ/4. However nodes at x = n λ/2 depend on boundary conditions; use the correct node spacing explanation.

questions.q: Spacing between adjacent nodes in a standing wave is:
questions.explanation: Adjacent nodes are separated by λ/2? Actually nodes occur every λ/2 in general for standing waves; adjacent node-to-node spacing is λ/2 and node-to-nearest-antinode is λ/4. (Choose the standard correct numeric.)

questions.q: For standing wave on a string with fixed ends separated by L, allowed wavelengths are λ_n = 2L/n. This implies fundamental frequency f1 = v/(2L).
questions.explanation: For a string fixed at both ends, nodes at ends give λ_n = 2L/n; f_n = n v/(2L).

questions.q: A string of length 1.0 m and wave speed 200 m/s carries a standing wave with n=2 (second harmonic). Frequency is:
Two waves y1 = 0.02 sin(20x - 200t) and y2 = 0.02 sin(20x + 200t) (SI) produce a standing wave. The amplitude at x=π/40 is approximately:
questions.explanation: Amplitude envelope = 2A cos(kx). k=20 �� cos(kx)=cos(20×π/40)=cos(π/2)=0 ⇒ amplitude 0 (node). If x chosen gives anticnode then 2A.

questions.q: In a progressive wave particles at different x are oscillating with:
questions.explanation: All particles oscillate at same frequency; phase varies with x and t according to kx - ωt.

questions.q: For y = A sin(kx - ωt), instantaneous transverse particle velocity v_y is:
questions.explanation: Particle transverse velocity v_y = ∂y/∂t = -A ω cos(kx - ωt) (sign depends on differentiation). Magnitude Aω cos(...).

questions.q: Wave number k and angular frequency ω relate to λ and f by:
options: k = v/λ and ω = v f
questions.explanation: k = 2π/λ and ω = 2π f.

questions.q: If two progressive waves have slightly different frequencies they produce:
questions.explanation: Waves of slightly different frequencies produce beats (modulation in amplitude) rather than a stationary wave.

questions.q: A stationary wave on a string of length 0.75 m has nodes at both ends and 3 antinodes (first 3 modes). The mode number n is:
questions.explanation: Number of antinodes = n. If 3 antinodes with fixed ends, n=3; wavelength λ = 2L/n = 2×0.75/3 = 0.5 m.

questions.q: Given a progressive wave y = 0.01 sin(8π x - 400π t) (SI), frequency f and wavelength λ are:
questions.explanation: ω = 400π ⇒ f = ω/(2π)=200 Hz. k = 8π ⇒ λ = 2π/k = 2π/(8π)=0.25? Wait compute: k=8π so λ=2π/(8π)=1/4=0.25 m. Check v=ω/k=(400π)/(8π)=50 m/s. (Pick option matching consistent values.)

questions.q: The expression y_total = 2A cos(kx) sin(ωt) implies that at a fixed x the motion is:
questions.explanation: At fixed x, y(t) = [2A cos(kx)] sin(ωt) → simple harmonic motion with amplitude 2A cos(kx).

questions.q: If two progressive waves of equal amplitude meet at a point and are in phase, the resultant amplitude is:
questions.explanation: Constructive interference (in phase) gives amplitude 2A.

questions.q: In a pure stationary wave the net energy transport along the medium is:
questions.explanation: Standing waves do not transport energy along the medium on average; energy oscillates between kinetic and potential locally.

questions.q: A point at an antinode in a standing wave has maximum:
questions.explanation: Antinode: maximum amplitude; Node: zero amplitude.

questions.q: Two progressive waves y1 = 0.05 sin(π x - 100π t) and y2 = 0.05 sin(π x + 100π t) give standing wave amplitude 0.10 cos(π x). The distance between adjacent nodes is:
questions.explanation: k = π ⇒ λ = 2π/k = 2. So λ = 2 m. Adjacent node spacing = λ/2 = 1 m. (Check values vs choices; choose the correct one based on computed λ.)

questions.q: For y = 2A cos(kx) sin(ωt), maximum transverse speed of a particle at x occurs when sin(ωt)=±1. Maximum speed magnitude is:
questions.explanation: y = 2A cos(kx) sin(ωt) ⇒ ∂y/∂t = 2A ω cos(kx) cos(ωt). Max (in magnitude) is 2A ω |cos(kx)| when cos(ωt)=±1.
